attachments.origin_landmark: cartilaginous part of the pharyngotympanic tube and the adjoining sphenoid

actions: tenses the tympanic membrane, damping the transmission of loud low-frequency sound

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Pulls the malleus handle medially. With stapedius it forms the acoustic reflex arc, which protects the inner ear from sustained loud noise but is too slow to protect against impulse noise such as gunfire.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique, and not typically injected in isolation. The only report of BoNT delivered directly to tensor tympani is a trans-canal microscopic middle-ear exploration in which the muscle is directly visualized and injected together with stapedius (both muscles line the posterior/medial tympanic cavity). Separately, several reports treat tensor-tympani-mediated tinnitus indirectly by injecting the tensor VELI PALATINI (a different, trigeminal-innervated muscle that shares CN V3 innervation and a reflex link to tensor tympani) via a transoral/trans-palatal route -- these do NOT inject tensor tympani itself and are recorded under tensor_veli_palatini instead.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Direct trans-canal route: needle tip placed on the visualized tensor tympani muscle/tendon in the anterior-medial tympanic cavity, near the cochleariform process where its tendon turns to insert on the malleus handle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Direct visualization via trans-canal microscopy/endoscopy confirms placement on the muscle itself; no EMG-based confirmation was described.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Middle ear myoclonus involving tensor tympani (with or without stapedius) is a rare cause of objective/clicking tinnitus, conventionally managed with medication (clonazepam, carbamazepine) or surgical tenotomy of the tensor tympani and/or stapedius tendons; a single case report used trans-canal BoNT injection as a reversible diagnostic/therapeutic trial before committing to surgery, with complete symptom resolution. This is not an established or common BoNT indication -- reported here as the one direct precedent found, with that caveat. A separate, more developed literature (see tensor_veli_palatini) treats the same symptom (objective/palatal tinnitus, forced-eyelid-closure-syndrome tinnitus) by injecting the tensor veli palatini rather than tensor tympani directly.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Hutz MJ, Aasen MH, Kircher M, 'A Novel Technique for the Diagnosis and Management of Middle Ear Myoclonus', Laryngoscope 131:E248-E249 (2021), doi:10.1002/lary.28579 -- retrieved via PubMed; Zhang-Kraczkowska A, Wong WK, 'Middle ear myoclonus: pathophysiology and management', Curr Opin Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 33(5):281-285 (2025), doi:10.1097/MOO.0000000000001073 -- retrieved via PubMed (review noting botulinum toxin, including intratympanic delivery, as an emerging but not yet standardized option for MEM).
